bib.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Information Extraction Capabilities: An Assessment of Performance, Explainability, Calibration, and Faithfulness

question: How well does ChatGPT do on seven information extraction tasks, and are its explanations, confidence scores and rationales explainable, calibrated and faithful?
contributions: Evaluate ChatGPT on four dimensions (performance, explainability, calibration, faithfulness), collecting 15 keys from ChatGPT or domain experts
Compare ChatGPT with BERT, RoBERTa and SOTA on Standard-IE and OpenIE settings
Release manually annotated test sets and code

method.summary: ChatGPT is prompted zero-shot via the official API on 14 IE datasets (7 tasks) with a single JSON-output prompt that asks for prediction, top-3/5, confidence 0-100, a reason and a self-judged reasonableness flag. Standard-IE gives a label set; OpenIE gives none and domain experts judge reasonableness. Human annotation on about 3,000 sampled items checks reasons and faithfulness.
method.task: information extraction (ET, NER, RC, RE, ED, EAE, EE) evaluation of ChatGPT

datasets.name: ACE05-E
datasets.size: 832 test (ED, EE), 403 (EAE); annotated 218 ED, 313 EAE, 552 EE

models.name: Per-dataset SOTA (PICOT, ACE, KLG, RIFRE, PL-Marker, SaliencyED, ONEIE, DEGREE)

inference.samples: inferred: one response per item; whole test sets queried via official API; conversation cleared after each response. Human evaluation on about 3,000 samples in total, roughly 200 per dataset
inference.prompting: Zero-shot instruction = task description + label set (Standard-IE only) + input and requirement asking for JSON with trigger/prediction, top3, top5, confidence (0-100), if_context_dependent, reason, if_reasonable. No demonstrations.

metrics.name: Micro-F1
metrics.definition: all tasks except RE and EE; RE reports NER F1 and relation F1, EE trigger F1 and argument F1

metrics.name: Accuracy (Standard-IE vs OpenIE)
metrics.definition: Standard: match to ground truth; OpenIE: 3 domain experts vote whether prediction is reasonable

metrics.name: top-k recall
metrics.definition: ground truth within ChatGPT's top 1/3/5 predicted labels

metrics.name: reasonable score
metrics.definition: share of correct-prediction samples whose reason is judged reasonable by ChatGPT (self-check) or 3 experts (human-check)

metrics.name: ECE
metrics.definition: expected calibration error, deviation of confidence from accuracy, 50 bins

metrics.name: faithfulness
metrics.definition: share of explanations not fictitious relative to input text, expert-annotated, for correct predictions

eval.protocol: Fine-tuned baselines cited from papers or re-implemented with official code; ChatGPT zero-shot. No repeated runs, seeds or significance test reported. Inter-annotator agreement not reported.

availability.data: manually annotated test sets released at same url

prompts.purpose: Event detection input, Standard-IE (three parts: task description, label set, input and requirement)
prompts.text: Task Description: Given an input list of words, identify all triggers in the list, and categorize each of them into the predefined set of event types. A trigger is the main word that most clearly expresses the occurrence of an event in the predefined set of event types. ... Input and Task Requirement: Perform ED task for the following input list, and print the output: [...] The output of ED task should be a list of dictionaries following json format. Each dictionary corresponds to the occurrence of an event in the input list and should consists of "trigger", "word_index", "event_type", "top3_event_type", "top5_event_type", "confidence", "if_context_dependent", "reason" and "if_reasonable" nine keys. ... Note that your answer should only contain the json string and nothing else.

limits: Closed model, version and date not stated; no decoding settings reported, so reruns are not exact
Only one concise unified prompt, no prompt variants or few-shot; authors note other work used domain prompts and got better IE results
Self-check reasonableness is by the same model, 100% so uninformative
Human evaluation by 3 experts on ~200 samples per dataset; no inter-annotator agreement; OpenIE accuracy is not comparable with F1 and does not require matching ground truth
Verbalised confidence, not token probabilities, used for ECE
Standard-IE ChatGPT choice of label set may be hurt by hard-to-understand labels
Explanations judged only for correct predictions
Results for early-2023 ChatGPT have dated

terms.definition: ChatGPT selects the most appropriate answer from a set of candidate labels, given task description, input text, prompt and label set
no candidate labels are given; ChatGPT relies solely on task description, prompt and input text
